name: get_customer
description: Look up one customer's full details (name, email, signup date) by their numeric id. Only use this when you already have the id. If you only know the customer's name, call search_customers first to get the id.

name: list_orders
description: List orders, most recent first. Optionally filter by customer id and/or status. Use this for questions about specific orders.

customer_id.description: Only orders for this customer id. Omit for all customers.

status.description: Only orders with this status. Omit for all statuses.

limit.description: Max orders to return. Defaults to 10.

name: revenue_by_product
description: Total revenue and units sold per product across all non-cancelled orders. Use for questions about sales, revenue, or best-selling products.

name: search_customers
description: Find customers by name when you do NOT already know their numeric id. Matches any part of the name, case-insensitive, so "acme" finds "Acme Corp". Returns each match's id, which you can then pass to tools that need one. Use this first whenever a question names a customer in words rather than by id.

name_contains.description: Part or all of the customer's name, e.g. "acme".

limit.description: Max customers to return. Defaults to 10.

name: list_products
description: List products in the catalogue with their price in cents and current stock level. Use for questions about what is sold, what something costs, or what is in stock. This does NOT include sales figures - for revenue or units sold, use revenue_by_product.

in_stock_only.description: If true, only products with stock above zero. Defaults to false.

limit.description: Max products to return. Defaults to 20.

name: top_customers
description: Rank customers by total amount spent across all non-cancelled orders, highest first. Use for questions about the biggest, best, or most valuable customers. For a per-product breakdown instead of per-customer, use revenue_by_product.

limit.description: How many customers to return. Defaults to 5.

name: cancel_order
description: Cancel a single PENDING order by its numeric id. This CHANGES data: it sets the order's status to 'cancelled' and cannot be undone. Only orders still in 'pending' status can be cancelled - shipped, delivered, or already-cancelled orders cannot. Use only when the user has clearly asked to cancel a specific order and you know its numeric id (call list_orders first if you only have a customer name).

order_id.description: The numeric id of the order to cancel, e.g. 2.
